- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model often holds too high; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending sideways, model tends to lag; forecast should be slightly ahead of 3–5 day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 14-day EWMA or sentiment-weighted average to smooth out noise.
